question: m12
q: Is electricity inflation running ahead of overall inflation?

transcript.answer:
Yes. Electricity inflation is running well ahead of overall inflation, though the gap has narrowed recently.

**Latest figures, August 2026 (year-on-year):**
- Electricity: **13.2%**
- All-groups CPI: **4.0%**
- Trimmed mean (the RBA's underlying measure): **3.6%**

Electricity prices are rising about 3.3 times as fast as headline inflation.

**How the gap has changed:**
- Electricity inflation peaked at 37.1% in October 2025 and hit 37.0% again in February 2026. It was still 21–22% in May and June 2026.
- It then dropped to 6.1% in July 2026, before rising to 13.2% in August.
- Headline CPI has ranged between 3.4% and 4.6% over the past year. It peaked at 4.6% in March 2026 and was 4.0% in August.

**Why the swings:** Electricity was falling 6.3% a year in June 2025. Government energy rebates were probably part of the reason. The 2025–26 jump likely reflects those rebates fading out of the annual comparison, along with underlying price rises. That is my inference, because the data doesn't show the cause. The July 2026 dip is probably a base effect from the July 2025 price reset. The August rebound shows the monthly figures are volatile.

Electricity is still adding noticeably to headline inflation. Headline CPI (4.0%) is above trimmed mean (3.6%), which fits with volatile items like electricity pushing the headline up.
